title: Euless Jean's background and the four-piece first band
summary: Jean was born in New Orleans the same year, studied with his uncle Nelson Jean; Dollier cannot recall the rest of the four-piece band.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Now to get back to your first job, which we sort of interrupted, you mentioned it was with Euless Jean. Do you know anything about him, where he came from? Was he from New Orleans itself or from the country?
Yeah, he was born in New Orleans and he was raised, we was raised, he was raised on Ayquart Street and I was raised on Bourbon Street.
Is he about your same age?
He's the same age as me. He was born in December.
And I'm born in October. Yeah.

Yeah, we're the same age. Same age. You know, if he took lessons from anybody? Yeah, he took lessons from his uncle, Nelson Jean. Oh, yeah, I never knew anything about him. I never did talk to Euless Jean either. No. And he may get down here though sometime, I guess you say he comes down here to work anyway. Yeah, if I ever see him, I'll have him to come see him. If he's ever here at night, tell him to come by the hall here. I sure will. A lot of people will be glad to see him, I know.
Yeah, I'm going to pass the word around to his brother when I see him.
A lot of people have heard of him, but does he play trumpet anymore?
No, I don't think. I don't know if he's interested in it or what, you know. Yeah.
But I'll talk to him about it. I just heard him play one night at a lawn party about 1944. Yeah. Who else was in the band, that first job you had?
Oh, I just can't remember that. It was a four-piece band. That's four pieces.
I just can't remember. They used clarinet or trombone?
It was a clarinet player, but I lost trace of him, who he was. I just can't remember him.
